20 Backlog #4 — Children: a home for the app's core entity, not a sub-tab of Enrollment

Children are what a daycare actually runs on, but the console had no dedicated place for them — a child only existed inside Enrollment, Attendance or Billing, never as a record of their own. This adds Children as a top-level section (now in the sidebar of every screen, between Staff and Rooms). 20a the roster — the section home, every child across rooms with setup and medical flags surfaced up front. 20b the medical & allergies register — the center-wide safety view no single feature owned. Each row opens the child profile (19a), and the other sections now point here: the "+ New" menu creates a child profile, and every feature that references a child links back to this record.

Help›Ratios
Fixing an over-ratio roomUpdated Jun 2026 · 2 min read
When a room's child-to-educator ratio goes above your licence limit, the dashboard flags it and the clock starts. Here's the fastest way to bring it back in line.
1Open the flagged room from the alert, or from Rooms & ratios in the sidebar.
2Tap Assign floater and pick an educator who's on shift and not tied to another room.
3The alert clears once the room is back in ratio. The whole event is kept in the audit log.
No one free? Split the room or move children to an in-ratio room — both keep you compliant while you call in cover.

Billing moved out of turn 2 into its own group. 6a the overview (moved from 2a). 6b a family statement — ledger, payment plan, autopay. 6c year-end tax forms: one statement per child, generated from the ledger and published straight to the parent app, so families claim the child-care credit without calling you. 6d that same form from the parent's side. Every action has a developed flow: 6e the statement PDF & publish, 6f fix a ledger mismatch, 6g reminders & payment plans, 6h autopay invites, 6i new invoice · receipt · exports, 6j rates & tax profile. Record-a-payment stays at 2c. Billing is feature-complete.
